newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson Multimedia net loss 3.1 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Multimedia net loss 3.1 bln Ffr.

text.p: Thomson SA unit Thomson Multimedia said it made a net loss after provisions for exceptional items of 3.1 billion francs in 1996.
It said in a statement its operating loss was 409 million francs.
Thomson Multimedia is the consumer electronics arm of state-owned Thomson SA and is slated for privatisation.
Sales totalled 37,767 million francs, up 3.6 percent.
Financial costs totalled 1,357 million and the group made an extraordinary restructuring provision of 1,295 million.

Last year was "a year of genuine crisis on the consumer electronics market", with a sharp downturn in the United States which saw a three percent drop in volume and five percent decline in prices, it said.
The market in Europe stagnated and had not recovered to 1990 levels, and saw a price erosion of five percent.
Western markets had gone through a deep recession and showed a break with the traditional average annual growth of three percent, it said.
After a particularly tough first half, second-half revenues rose eight percent and showed a positive operating result of more than 600 million francs.
The results did not yet reflect an expected state capital injection or the recovery of patent revenues, it said.
The state is due to put around 11 billion francs into Thomson Multimedia.

"With a more attractive balance sheet and new patent revenues, and benefiting from the effects of restructuring decisions now being implemented, the way ahead for the company should be clear within two years," it said.
